subject: Evaluation gates, acceptance credits and on‑prem licensing for Optima pilot
messages:
From: Jay Singh <j.singh@optimahealth.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@optimahealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluation plan + commercial mechanics for Private Pilot

Maya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Optima is aligned to run a private/VPC pilot to validate performance and security before a broader rollout. Procurement asked me to put some high‑level asks on the table so we can scope internal approvals:

- 60–90 day pilot, private VPC with data residency in us‑west.
- Acceptance checkpoints (functional test, latency/SLO, security/compliance signoff).
- We need clarity on pilot credits, any platform fees during pilot, and what triggers a paid commit.
- Pricing transparency for reserved capacity (commits) vs on‑prem perpetual license + support.

Can you share a mutual action plan (MAP) that maps acceptance gates to commercial milestones (credits, discounts, commit ramp) and a list of required artifacts for security review? Attached is a rough eval plan from our engineering team (Optima_EvalPlan.xlsx).

Looking to have an LOI/decision framework by mid‑May.

Regards,
Jay Singh
Head of Platform Engineering
Optima Health

---
Attachment: Optima_EvalPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 87KB)

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: Jay Singh <j.singh@optimahealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan + commercial mechanics for Private Pilot

Jay —

Appreciate the clear asks and the eval plan. I've drafted a concise MAP and initial commercial scaffold for the pilot and post‑pilot options. High level summary:

Pilot scope and gates (proposed):
1) Gate A — Functionality & output quality (end of week 3): pass/fail tests on 10 canonical workflows. Acceptance unlocks onboarding credit.
2) Gate B — Latency & SLO (end of week 6): 99th percentile latency targets and throughput validated under expected load. Passing unlocks acceptance credit and reduced token pricing for ramp.
3) Gate C — Security & compliance (by day 90): SOC2 evidence, network proofs, successful data residency checks. Passing triggers recommended commit terms and extended pricing caps.

Commercial scaffolding (pilot -> commit):
- Pilot credit: $25,000 applied to usage during the pilot.
- Gate A credit: additional $10,000 on successful functional acceptance.
- Gate B credit: additional $20,000 on latency acceptance.
- Platform fee during pilot: waived for first 60 days; after that a nominal platform fee (monthly) applies unless a LOI to reserve capacity is signed.
- Post‑pilot options: reserved capacity (monthly commit) or one‑time on‑prem license + annual support. We can provide side‑by‑side economics in the MAP doc.

I attached a one‑page MAP (Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf) with the milestone schedule and required artifacts for your security team.

Next steps: if this is directionally acceptable, I will loop Marcus to finalize concession language and coordinate legal for a non‑binding LOI template. Would Procurement be ok with a 2‑week review once we hand over the MAP?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk through.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0113

---
Attachment: Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (map, 120KB)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-07T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan + commercial mechanics for Private Pilot

Maya —

Thanks for drafting. A few commercial notes I recommend before sharing a formal LOI:

1) Platform fee waiver: reduce default waiver to 60 days (from "first 60 days" it's ok) but offer an extended waiver (additional 30 days) if Optima signs a non‑binding LOI committing to >=30% reserved capacity within 30 days of pilot close.

2) Acceptance credits: keep $25k total but reallocate to $15k (Gate A) / $10k (Gate B) to better reflect engineering effort and to link ramp economics to Gate B performance.

3) Pricing cap: offer a 6‑month price cap after commit to protect Optima from model upgrades that materially change token economics; cap requires minimum 12‑month commitment.

4) On‑prem licensing: propose two paths — SaaS VPC with monthly platform fee, or perpetual license with 12% annual support fee. For on‑prem, require a one‑time installation fee and an annual maintenance SLA.

5) Require SOC2 summary and any external penetration test results before Gate C acceptance; we should proactively provide SOC2_summary.pdf.

If you want, I can draft the pricing clauses and LOI language. Happy to set up a call with Sales Engineering to align on measurement metrics for Gate B.

-Marcus
Director, Commercials, Redwood Inference

From: Jay Singh <j.singh@optimahealth.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@optimahealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan + commercial mechanics for Private Pilot

Maya / Marcus —

Thank you for the thoughtful proposal. A few quick counterpoints from Procurement and Platform leadership:

- Platform fee waiver: Procurement prefers a 90‑day waive during pilot. Alternatively, a 60‑day waive + guaranteed 3‑month cap on platform fee post‑pilot is acceptable.
- Commitment trigger: Optima can provide a non‑binding LOI, but we prefer a ramp schedule with a 25% reserved capacity target by month 6 and 50% by month 12 (rather than a single upfront percent).
- Acceptance credits look good but Procurement wants acceptance credits to apply against the first 12 months of committed spend (not only pilot).
- Security: we need SOC2 report and a short data residency attestation. Also need a quick RFI response — attaching our procurement packet (Procurement_RFI.docx).

If you can update the MAP to reflect a 90‑day pilot with the ramp schedule and show economics for both SaaS VPC and on‑prem license (TCO over 24 months), we can take to Procurement leadership next week.

Regards,
Jay Singh
---
Attachment: Procurement_RFI.docx (docx, 45KB)

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: Jay Singh <j.singh@optimahealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, procurement@optimahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-20T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP proposal: credits, ramp ladder, and licensing options (Optima)

Jay / Procurement team —

Per our thread and the attached updated MAP (Optima_MAP_v2.pdf), here is the updated commercial proposal and milestone mapping. I tried to balance Optima's need for runway with Redwood's requirement for a clear ramp commitment to unlock deeper credits/discounts.

Summary (Updated MAP v2):
- Pilot length: 90 days private VPC (data residency: us‑west).
- Pilot credits: $25,000 applied to pilot usage.
- Acceptance credits: $15,000 on Gate A (functional), $25,000 on Gate B (latency/SLO), both credits are applied to first 12 months of committed spend if a commit is signed within 45 days of Gate B.
- Platform fee: waived for first 60 days; waive extended to 90 days if Optima signs a non‑binding LOI committing to a 24‑month ramp plan (25% month 6, 50% month 12). If LOI is not signed, platform fee applies after day 60 at standard monthly rate.
- Post‑pilot pricing options:
  a) SaaS VPC reserved capacity: tiered discounts based on committed monthly spend; 24‑month term recommended to achieve deepest per‑token price.
  b) On‑prem perpetual license: one‑time license fee + 12% annual support; requires installation and acceptance testing window (Gate B equivalent).
- Pricing cap: 6‑month cap on per‑token price increases after commit for customers who sign >=12‑month commitment.

Security and artifacts requested: SOC2_summary.pdf (attached), network topology, and penetration test report (if available). We'll provide SOC2_summary.pdf and a short data residency attestation.

Next steps:
1) If this aligns, sign the non‑binding LOI by 2027‑05‑04 to secure the 90‑day waiver + pathway to extended discounts. LOI (one‑pager) and DocuSign link here: https://redwood.app/docusign/ABC123
2) Redwood SE will produce a TCO comparison (SaaS VPC vs on‑prem) and a Gate B measurement plan by 2027‑04‑27.
3) Legal teams to exchange redlines on the licensing exhibit once LOI is in place.

Attachments: Optima_MAP_v2.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to set a working session early next week to walk the MAP with Platform and Procurement.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0113
